_meta.purpose: Model-agnostic character identity + wardrobe lock for the LOCAL open-weight rebuild of the 43.000 s / 1290-frame vertical reel. Method is still-per-scene -> image-to-video -> mux the existing master music. Nothing here names a model, sampler, LoRA, node graph or resolution: it states WHAT must be in frame.
_meta.scope: 11 macro scenes, 2 characters (M1, F1), 2 sets (SET_A red studio, SET_B desert quarry)
authoritative_sources: 05_HIGGSFIELD_RECREATION_SETUP.md Appendix A (the two literal character blocks)
05_HIGGSFIELD_RECREATION_SETUP.md §1 (why the leads are archetypes and not the real actors' faces)

naming_policy.rule: No real person's name and no named TV character appears in any description, prompt_block or anchor field of this sheet. Characters are addressed by code only: M1 and F1.

invented_labels_kept_out_of_prompts.M1: the upstream files give M1 an invented given name; it is deliberately not reproduced here because an invented proper noun adds nothing to an image model and can collide with a real person who happens to share it

naming_policy.forbidden_token_gate: marketing/campaigns/peshta/05_build/bin/ipgate.sh greps prompts/ for alemdar|kurtlar|vadisi|sasmaz|şaşmaz|pana film|sobirov|xamdam|hamdam|peshta|valley of the wolves|deepfake|face swap|lookalike|looks exactly like|celebrity|shot-for-shot and exits non-zero on a hit. Run the same gate over the local prompt set before generating.

source_conflict_resolution.question: Do the actual prompt files and character sheets describe real people, or original archetypes?
source_conflict_resolution.answer: BOTH, in two separate and incompatible generations of the work. They are not the same design, and they never were reconciled.

generation_1_real_names.what_they_say: The leads are named as two characters from a 2003-2005 Turkish TV series, each annotated with the real actor who plays them, and the positive prompts instruct the model to 'embody' those named characters in that named series' aesthetic.
generation_1_real_names.physical_design: male: early 30s, swept-back pompadour, clean-shaven with 5 o'clock shadow, bespoke midnight-black two-button suit, white open-collar shirt / canyon variant with felt fedora + navy pilot bomber. female: 26, chocolate brunette cascading waves, hazel eyes, ivory silk tea-length dress or cream turtleneck + charcoal blazer.
generation_1_real_names.status: This is the design of the EXISTING cloud reel, final_polat_peshta_reel.mp4 (see FINAL_RECREATION_REPORT.md §1 and §3 - 11 macro shots, hf_mult_motion_control).

generation_2_original_archetypes.what_they_say: Explicitly 'original fictional character'. No series, no actor, no character name anywhere - enforced by a grep gate. Each lead carries ONE invented asymmetric anchor feature (his scar, her beauty mark) whose stated job is twofold: shot-to-shot consistency, and making the face demonstrably nobody's.
generation_2_original_archetypes.physical_design: male: 38, very short matte crop, dense 8 mm trimmed beard, charcoal-black frock coat, bare-headed. female: 31, flat centre-parted nape knot, ivory column gown, net veil.
generation_2_original_archetypes.status: This is the design of the parallel 32-cut local-gate build (05_build/BUILD_COMPLETE.md), and it is the design this sheet adopts.

source_conflict_resolution.which_this_sheet_follows: Generation 2, unconditionally. The task requires archetype-only description fields, and generation 2 is additionally the newer, gated, and physically self-consistent set. Every real-name reference found in generation 1 is recorded in provenance_flags below rather than silently dropped.
source_conflict_resolution.ab_comparability_caveat: The cloud reel being A/B'd wears generation 1's wardrobe. A rebuild in generation 2's wardrobe is a fair test of the local MODEL STACK but not a pixel-matched costume comparison. wardrobe_by_set.ab_parity_variant gives a name-free, costume-generic alternative if a closer visual match is wanted; read its caution first.

M1.role: male lead / the one who sings to the lens
M1.archetype: Anatolian crime-drama antihero - a genre type, not a person: composed, watchful, under-expressive, authority carried by stillness rather than motion
M1.height_build: 180 cm, lean athletic, broad square shoulders, upright, no bulk
M1.complexion: medium-tan Mediterranean, matte, visible pores, natural asymmetry, no beauty filter
M1.face_shape: oval with a broad flat brow, high flat cheekbones, strong square jaw
M1.eyes: deep-set dark brown under heavy straight black brows, level unblinking gaze, muted catchlights
M1.nose: aquiline with a slight break at the bridge
M1.hair: black, cropped very short at the sides, slightly longer on top, matte, no styling product
M1.facial_hair: short dense trimmed black beard, 8 mm, sharp cheek line, no moustache flare
M1.anchor_feature: a short vertical scar through the outer third of the LEFT eyebrow
M1.anchor_feature_screen_side: his LEFT = image RIGHT on a frontal frame. Verified this way at GATE 1; 3 of 4 auditions failed by mirroring it. Check the side on every still.
M1.expression_register: flat and closed: no smile, no eyebrow raise, no head tilt, no visible teeth. Emotion is conveyed by chin drop and eye lift, nothing else.
M1.posture_default: weight on the back foot, hips square to camera, shoulders level and still, chin dropped ~10 degrees, eyes lifted to the lens, hands low and open
M1.props: worn amber prayer beads hanging from the left hand with the thumb resting on them; heavy oxidised silver signet ring with a geometric eight-point star on the right ring finger; plain steel watch on a cracked brown leather strap
M1.prompt_block: original fictional character, Turkish man, 38 years old, lean athletic build, 180 cm, broad square shoulders, medium-tan Mediterranean complexion; oval face with a broad flat brow, deep-set dark brown eyes under heavy straight black brows, aquiline nose with a slight break at the bridge, high flat cheekbones, strong square jaw, thin unsmiling mouth; a short vertical scar through the outer third of the LEFT eyebrow; black hair cropped very short at the sides, slightly longer on top, matte, no styling product; short dense trimmed black beard, 8 mm, sharp cheek line, no moustache flare; no glasses, no earrings, no tattoos, no visible teeth; visible skin pores, natural asymmetry, matte unretouched skin, no beauty filter
M1.prompt_block_notes: Paste verbatim into every scene still, unedited and unparaphrased. Re-describing the face per scene is what produces 11 different men.

F1.archetype: glamorous dynastic antagonist - a genre type, not a person: power expressed by not moving, by making people wait, by being looked at without returning warmth
F1.age_band: 30-33, reads early 30s; never a 20s ingenue face
F1.height_build: tall, long-necked, straight level shoulders, slim
F1.complexion: pale olive, matte, visible pores, natural asymmetry, unretouched, no beauty filter
F1.face_shape: oval, very high cheekbones, delicate pointed chin
F1.eyes: large hooded dark-brown with a level gaze, muted catchlights
F1.mouth: full and unsmiling, deep berry lip, never showing teeth
F1.hair: black, centre-parted, pulled back flat and low into a small nape knot; no loose waves, no volume
F1.anchor_feature: a small dark beauty mark high on the RIGHT cheekbone, below the outer eye
F1.anchor_feature_screen_side: her RIGHT = image LEFT on a frontal frame. Verified this way at GATE 1; 3 of 4 auditions failed by mirroring it. Check the side on every still.
F1.expression_register: cool and withholding: no smile, no lean-in, chin level. Gaze to the lens, then drifting slowly off-camera left.
F1.posture_default: seated upright on the red carpeted riser, spine long, knees together and angled away from camera, hands folded still in the lap
F1.props: none in hand by default; anything handed to her (flowers, a strand) is received, never grasped tightly
F1.prompt_block: original fictional character, Turkish woman, 31 years old, tall and long-necked, straight level shoulders, slim; pale olive skin; oval face, very high cheekbones, large hooded dark-brown eyes with a level gaze, long straight narrow nose, full unsmiling mouth, delicate pointed chin; a small dark beauty mark high on the RIGHT cheekbone below the outer eye; black hair, centre-parted, pulled back flat and low into a small nape knot; minimal makeup, matte skin, deep berry lip, no visible teeth; visible skin pores, natural asymmetry, unretouched, no beauty filter
F1.prompt_block_notes: Paste verbatim into every scene still, unedited and unparaphrased.

SET_A.name: red studio
SET_A.description: monochrome red-orange seamless cyclorama studio, matte orange foam blocks scattered across the floor, a low red-carpeted rostrum of three broad risers; a corps of sixteen dancers in floor-length black dresses and black wide-brim hats
SET_A.formation_lateral: the corps stands in a symmetric bank spreading to both the left and right edges of the frame, the outer figures cut off by the frame edge so the line reads as continuing off screen
SET_A.formation_depth: the corps in four receding rows behind the subject, not in a lateral line
SET_A.light: single hard warm key from camera-left 45 degrees, deep red gel wash on the background, hot specular edge along the jaw, heavy falloff, no fill
SET_A.screen_time: 0.000-25.496 s and 35.896-43.000 s of the 43.000 s piece (cloud reel shots 01-07, 10, 11)

SET_B.name: desert quarry
SET_B.description: eroded sand-cliff quarry exterior under a pale bleached sky, freestanding red-painted rectangular gate frames standing vertically in the sand, red blocks scattered; a corps in all-white suits with plain white lace masks fully covering their faces
SET_B.light: open noon daylight, bleached highlights, hard short shadows, no fill

frame_invariants_both_sets.lens: 50 mm anamorphic feel, T2.0, shallow depth of field, subject centred in a vertical 9:16 frame, eyeline at 38 percent from the top of frame
frame_invariants_both_sets.grade: filmic, warm, crushed blacks, fine 35 mm grain, slight halation on highlights, saturated red channel

SET_A.description: charcoal-black heavy wool frock coat, high standing collar, worn closed, double row of matte black horn buttons, long skirt to mid-thigh, no insignia, no epaulettes, no braid, no medals; black shirt buttoned to the throat, no tie; a narrow oxblood silk sash at the waist; bare-headed, the only uncovered head in the frame
SET_A.why_it_is_shaped_this_way: bare-headed against sixteen wide-brim hats makes the lead the single focal point at Reels scale; it is also the deliberate opposite of the source video's costume logic

SET_B.description: the same charcoal-black wool frock coat worn open over a slate-grey shirt buttoned to the collar, sand dust on the hem, bare-headed, collar turned up against the light
SET_B.continuity_note: same coat as SET_A, opened and dusted - it must read as one garment across the world change

SET_A.description: floor-length ivory silk column gown, high boat neckline, long narrow sleeves, matte crepe, bias cut; one heavy single-strand chain of dark garnet beads falling to the waist; a fine ivory net veil pinned low across the eyes to the cheekbone from a plain flat chignon, no cap, no beading; bare hands, no watch, no rings
SET_A.anchor_conflict: the net veil sits low across the eyes and can hide the RIGHT-cheekbone beauty mark. On close framings raise the veil line above the cheekbone or drop it entirely, or the anchor cannot be gate-checked.
SET_A.used_in_scenes: all F1 scenes in the 11-scene rebuild

SET_B.description: ivory tailored trouser suit, sharp shoulder, ivory silk shell, plain ivory net half-mask over the upper face
SET_B.used_in_scenes: none in the 11-scene cloud reel - F1 does not appear in the quarry block. Kept for parity only; if a local scene places her there, this is her garment.

ab_parity_variant.purpose: Optional. Only if the A/B must compare costume-for-costume against the existing cloud reel rather than model-stack against model-stack.
ab_parity_variant.caution: The cloud reel's wardrobe is a transcription of a named TV character's costume design, and the setup document's §1 rejects costume transcription as a derivative-work exposure separate from the likeness question - one a proper-noun grep gate does not catch. Use this only with explicit sign-off, and keep it generic as written below.
ab_parity_variant.M1_SET_A: dark two-button single-breasted wool suit, notch lapels, matching flat-front trousers, plain white cotton shirt worn open at the collar, no tie, black leather oxfords, plain belt, bare-headed, no sunglasses
ab_parity_variant.M1_SET_B: dark felt brimmed hat worn low, heavy navy-and-black zip-front flight jacket with a structured collar, white shirt collar showing at the neck, charcoal wool trousers
ab_parity_variant.F1_SET_A: plain ivory silk tea-length dress, modest boat neckline, clean tailoring, low ivory ankle-strap heels, a single strand of pale round beads held at the chest, no other jewellery
ab_parity_variant.identity_rule_unchanged: even in this variant the FACE stays the archetype face defined in characters.M1 and characters.F1 - wardrobe is the only thing that changes

consistency_anchors.how_to_use: These blocks are copied verbatim - byte-for-byte, same word order - into every one of the 11 scene stills. They are not a summary of the character fields above; they ARE the text that goes in the prompt. Paraphrase is the single largest cause of identity drift across independently generated stills. Scene-specific text (action, framing, set, light) is appended after the block, never interleaved into it.
consistency_anchors.ordering_rule: identity block -> wardrobe block -> props/posture -> action -> set -> light -> lens -> grade. Keep this order in all 11 prompts; changing clause order changes the weighting in most text-conditioned image models.

cross_scene_rules: One identity block per character, frozen for the whole build. Only wardrobe, set, light, lens and camera move change between scenes.
Never let a scene prompt restate a facial feature in different words - it competes with the block.
Carry the same anchor check into the image-to-video step: a still that passes can still drift once animated, so re-check the last frame of every generated clip.
Both characters keep a closed mouth and no teeth throughout; a smile is an identity break, not just a performance note.
Neither character wears a hat in any scene; hats belong to the corps only.
